slides.alt: Cover. High performance, applied. Wanting to improve isn’t a plan. Two behaviour studies, applied to runbooks. Swipe.

01, follow-through. Setting the challenge isn’t enough. 377 students, 15 weeks. Those who chose challenges and didn’t complete them changed in the opposite direction to the one they wanted. Source: Hudson and colleagues, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.

02, if-then. Decide the trigger in advance. Students owed a report about their Christmas Eve, due within two days. With an if-then plan, 71% delivered. Without, 32%. Source: Gollwitzer and Brandstätter, 1997; 36 students.
03, runbooks. A runbook is an if-then. If this alert fires, this person does this first. Anything vaguer is a wish, written down.
04, the cab. Find the cab. Tharp’s ritual was never the workout. It was hailing the cab. In an incident, the cab is declaring it. Source: Twyla Tharp, The Creative Habit.
